name: Vile Familiar Head
summary: Near the Burning Blade Coven, Vile Familiar Heads mark a grim test for young Horde warlocks. Under Ruzan's guidance, they gather the gruesome trophies as proof of readiness to bind their first demonic minions. The test demands discipline and respect for the lethality of the beings they mean to summon.

sections.title: A Gruesome Lesson in Demonology
sections.body: In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Ruzan asks novices seeking to learn summoning to bring him six Vile Familiar Heads. Vile familiars are fiery imps with dangerous elemental cunning, found outside the Burning Blade Coven. Novices must face and defeat them, proving they can subdue demonic life rather than be overcome by it. Warlocks are barely tolerated within Thrall's Horde, so their training calls for care. A novice slain by a conjured creature only deepens the dishonor and suspicion cast upon practitioners of the dark arts.

faq.q: What are Vile Familiar Heads used for?
faq.answer: The heads prove a novice warlock's readiness in the Valley of Trials. Ruzan requires six before teaching an apprentice to summon a first imp minion.

faq.q: Where do vile familiars come from?
faq.answer: Vile familiars gather at the mouth and inside a cave northeast within the Valley of Trials. The cave holds the secretive and malevolent Burning Blade Coven.

faq.q: Why does Ruzan make young warlocks collect these heads?
faq.answer: Ruzan expects a warlock to overpower a creature before summoning it. Imps are deceptive and throw volatile fire, so defeating them face-to-face teaches apprentices the danger of the demons they mean to command.

faq.q: How does the Horde view warlocks who collect such trophies?
faq.answer: The modern Horde tolerates warlocks without embracing them. Betrayals tied to fel magic left deep distrust, so Ruzan and other trainers insist apprentices study with discipline and discretion.

angles.text: For a warlock, collecting these heads is an early step toward mastery over the Nether and the right to summon and bind an imp into servitude.
Even in Durotar's training grounds, warlocks practice on the fringes, mindful of the lingering suspicion with which the Horde watches their demonic pursuits.
